issues.description: Credit card data (cardNumber, expiryDate, cvv) is stored in plain text in memory and passed through the application. This violates PCI DSS compliance and exposes sensitive payment information.
issues.suggestion: Never store or handle full card details in your application. Use a PCI-compliant payment processor (Stripe, Square, PayPal) with tokenization. Only store the last 4 digits and token reference.

issues.description: Card number validation only checks length (16 characters) without verifying the Luhn algorithm. This allows invalid card numbers to pass validation.
issues.suggestion: Implement Luhn algorithm validation: `function luhnCheck(num) { let sum = 0, isEven = false; for (let i = num.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) { let digit = parseInt(num[i], 10); if (isEven) digit *= 2; if (digit > 9) digit -= 9; sum += digit; isEven = !isEven; } return sum % 10 === 0; }`

issues.description: Expiry date validation has a year 2000 offset bug. Cards expiring in 2025 are parsed as year 2025 (correct), but the logic `2000 + parseInt(year)` assumes 2-digit years. This fails for years beyond 2099 and is fragile.
issues.suggestion: Use proper date parsing: `const currentYear = new Date().getFullYear() % 100; const expiryYear = parseInt(year); const fullYear = currentYear > expiryYear ? 2000 + expiryYear + 100 : 2000 + expiryYear;`

issues.description: Database query uses parameterized queries correctly, but the payment processing stores minimal information (only last 4 digits). There's no idempotency protection - the same request could charge twice.
issues.suggestion: Implement idempotency keys: require clients to send a unique idempotency_key and store processed keys in the database to prevent duplicate charges.

issues.description: JSON.parse() on line 158 and line 184 can throw an error if the stored data is invalid/corrupted. No try-catch handling exists.
issues.suggestion: Wrap JSON.parse in try-catch: `let features; try { features = JSON.parse(subscription.features); } catch (e) { console.error('Invalid features JSON:', e); features = []; }`

issues.description: The features array is duplicated in two places (lines 132-134 for premium/enterprise logic). This violates DRY principle and creates maintenance burden.
issues.suggestion: Create a configuration object: `const TIER_FEATURES = { premium: [...], enterprise: [...] }; const features = TIER_FEATURES[tier];`

issues.description: File contains critical payment processing logic with explicit warnings of no test coverage. This is unacceptable for production code handling financial transactions.
issues.suggestion: Before merging, write comprehensive unit and integration tests covering: valid/invalid card validation, payment processing success/failure, subscription state changes, edge cases (expired cards, timezone issues), and idempotency.

issues.description: No rate limiting on payment processing function. An attacker could spam payment attempts, potentially causing financial loss or fraud.
issues.suggestion: Implement rate limiting: track failed attempts per user/IP and enforce exponential backoff after N failures within a time window.

issues.description: Pricing logic includes hardcoded tax rate (8%) and processing fee (2.9%) that may vary by region/jurisdiction but aren't configurable.
issues.suggestion: Move pricing constants to configuration file or environment variables: `const TAX_RATE = parseFloat(process.env.TAX_RATE || '0.08');`

issues.description: The subscription validity check uses `validUntil < new Date()` but doesn't account for timezone differences or precise timing. A subscription expiring at midnight could be treated inconsistently.
issues.suggestion: Use ISO 8601 timestamps consistently and store dates in UTC: `if (new Date(subscription.valid_until).getTime() < Date.now()) { return false; }`

issues.description: No input validation on userId parameter. If used in string concatenation elsewhere or logged unsanitized, could cause injection issues. No checks for SQL injection from row data.
issues.suggestion: Validate userId format: `if (!/^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,255}$/.test(userId)) throw new Error('Invalid userId');` and validate all query results before use.

codeQuality.summary: This premium payment module contains multiple critical security vulnerabilities unsuitable for production. Primary concerns: (1) Raw credit card storage violates PCI DSS - must use tokenization with external payment processor; (2) No test coverage on critical financial logic; (3) Missing idempotency protection allows duplicate charges; (4) Insufficient card validation (no Luhn check); (5) No rate limiting on payment attempts; (6) JSON parsing without error handling; (7) Year 2000 offset bug in date validation. The code requires substantial security hardening, comprehensive test coverage, and architectural changes before any production deployment.

testCoverage.summary: CRITICAL: This file has zero test coverage and contains highly sensitive payment processing and security-critical access control logic. All 6 exported and internal functions require comprehensive test suites. Priority gaps include: (1) Payment processing with validation, pricing, and transaction recording; (2) Payment card validation with format and expiry checks; (3) Subscription management with feature assignment; (4) Feature access control with expiry boundary conditions; (5) Multiple edge cases around date calculations, JSON parsing, and database interactions. The lack of tests creates significant risks for financial transactions, unauthorized feature access, and data integrity issues. Immediate action required to add test coverage before this code reaches production.

refactorings.summary: This premium features module has significant refactoring opportunities focused on separation of concerns and testability. The highest-impact changes are: (1) Extract PaymentProcessor class to encapsulate payment-related logic (validation, pricing, charging), and (2) Extract SubscriptionRepository class for data access operations. These improve testability, maintainability, and enable proper mocking. Additionally, simplify the tier features mapping, extract expiry and validity check functions, and apply the Strategy pattern for payment processing orchestration. These refactorings directly address the critical test coverage gaps noted in comments and follow SOLID principles. Estimated effort: 4-6 hours for comprehensive refactoring; benefit: significantly improved testability and maintainability of business-critical payment logic.
